title: Cost Allocation Tags & Consolidated Billing 🏷️
description: Organise your spending with tags, enable chargebacks, and manage multiple accounts under one bill.

slides.title: Cost Allocation Tags: Who Spent What? 🏷️
slides.content:
# Labels That Track Spending

Tags are key‑value pairs you attach to AWS resources. **Cost allocation tags** are a specific type used to track costs in your billing reports.

- **AWS generated tags**: automatically created (e.g., `createdBy`).
- **User‑defined tags**: you define (e.g., `Environment=Production`, `Team=Payments`, `Project=Alpha`).

After you activate a tag for cost allocation (in Billing console), it appears in Cost Explorer and AWS Cost and Usage Reports. It takes up to 24 hours for tags to appear.

**Analogy**: Tags are like categories in a personal finance app. Without them, all your AWS spend is one big lump. With them, you can see exactly how much the "Dev" environment cost vs "Prod".

quizData.question: After creating a user‑defined tag, what must you do to see it in Cost Explorer?

options.text: Activate the tag for cost allocation in the Billing console
Apply the tag to the root account

quizData.explanation: Tags must be activated in the Cost Allocation Tags section before they are included in billing reports.

slides.title: AWS Organizations & Consolidated Billing 🏢
slides.content:
# One Bill, Many Accounts

With AWS Organizations, you can consolidate billing across multiple accounts:
- One **management account** pays for all member accounts.
- Volume discounts apply across all accounts (e.g., S3 storage tiering).
- Easier to track costs per account (each account is a separate cost dimension).
- Can use **Service Control Policies (SCPs)** to enforce cost‑related restrictions (e.g., deny EC2 usage in expensive regions).

**Best practice**: Create separate accounts for dev, test, prod, and security. Consolidate billing under a single management account.

slides.title: Chargebacks and Showbacks 💳
slides.content:
# Who Pays?

Using cost allocation tags and consolidated billing, you can implement:
- **Showback**: show teams their costs without actually billing them (drives accountability).
- **Chargeback**: actually bill internal teams based on their AWS usage.

Tools:
- AWS Cost Explorer with tags and accounts.
- AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR) – detailed, hourly/daily CSV in S3. Can be ingested into BI tools like QuickSight.
- Third‑party tools (CloudHealth, Apptio) for advanced chargeback workflows.

slides.title: AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR) 📄
slides.content:
# The Deepest Dive

The CUR is the most detailed billing dataset. Configured in the Billing console, it delivers a CSV (or Parquet) file to an S3 bucket daily or hourly. Contains:
- Every line item (resource ID, usage amount, cost).
- Tags and account IDs.
- Pricing details (On‑Demand, Reserved, Spot).

Use CUR to:
- Build custom dashboards in QuickSight.
- Analyse with Athena (SQL directly on S3).
- Feed into third‑party cost management tools.

Enabling CUR does not incur additional cost (except S3 storage/Athena queries).
